To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fibronectin EDA and EDB domains were not useful markers of oral malignancy.
the expression of different fibronectins in normal and pathological tissues is complex and not easily explained by the current understanding of fibronectins' roles in cell biology and pathology.
fibronectin has multiple functions, and that the expression of different fibronectins in different tissues and cell types is regulated by a number of mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that regulate the expression of fibronectins in the oral environment.
the role of fibronectins in the pathogenesis of oral squamous cell carcinomas and the development of oral dysplasias.
the role of fibronectins in cell-matrix interactions and their potential use as diagnostic and prognostic markers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EDA or the EDB domains do not appear to be specific markers of malignancy, but that further investigation of IIICS splice patterns may be of value.

RT-PCR-based analysis of fibronectins does not appear to be a suitable method for differentiating malignant from non-malignant oral mucosa, and that further studies are required to elucidate the biological significance of the different fibronectins splice variants.
the RT-PCR-based identification of either EDA+ or EDB+ fibronectin isoforms is not a marker of malignancy in the oral cavity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of fibronectins in oral squamous cell carcinomas, oral leukoplaki and reactive overgrowths is similar to that in normal oral mucosal tissue, and therefore, fibronectins are unlikely to have a role in the pathogenesis of these oral mucosal lesions.
there is no single splice variant that can be used to diagnose oral malignancy.
fibronectin is an important protein in oral cancer, and that its isoform expression is altered in oral cancer, but it is not a useful marker for oral cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no evidence that the expression of EDA or EDA+ fibronectin is associated with oral malignancy.
the EDA and EDB domains are not useful as markers of malignancies.
fibronectin is a very important molecule in the oral cavity and it is important to understand its role in oral cancer.
